summary: Kenryu T. Tsuji was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Bukkyo University and held professorships at Koyasan University (1926), Seizan College, Shuchiin University (1955), and Ryukoku University (emeritus, 1956), also teaching at Bukkyo University in 1952.
Kenryū Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University and served as professor emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014).
Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University around 1971 to 1975 and served as a professor there from around 2000 to 2018.

Kenta Suzuki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, later serving as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2012.

Kenyu Mitomo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Rissho University, UC Berkeley, and under Akira Hirakawa and others. At Rissho University, he served as Dean of Buddhist Studies (1968–2015) and Director of the Lotus Sutra Institute.

Kevin Alan Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his doctoral degree under Jeffrey Hopkins in 1997, and studied under Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and was doctoral supervised by Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

Khakyab Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Khenchen Tashi Özer, Tsuklak Nyinjé, Mingyur Wanggyel, and Sheja Künkhyen.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga, and he taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as abbot of Oxford Buddha Vihara, fellow at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, and professor at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Jampel Gyepai Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche Monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, later chairing the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Thegchog Dorje, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Khakyab Dorje and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, serving as Abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1976–2023), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–2023), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.

Khenpo Appey was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Drakgyab Lodrö. He served as Principal (1972–1985) and Director (attested 1991) of Sakya College, and held a post at Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
